children: Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend of $0.10 Per Share
MCLEAN, Va., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Primis Financial Corp. (

) ("Primis" or the "Company"), and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Primis Bank (the "Bank"), today reported net income available to common shareholders of $8.7 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income available to common shareholders of $6.8 million, or $0.28 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.  For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income available to common shareholders of $25.4 million, or $1.03 per diluted share, compared to net income available to common shareholders of $31.9 million, or $1.29 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Operating net income available to common shareholders(1) was $8.7 million, or $0.35 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, up 27% from operating net income available to common shareholders(1) of $6.8 million, or $0.28 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.  Year-to-date results in 2026 and 2025 benefited from investment gains of $5.9 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $32.0 million in the second quarter of 2025.  Excluding these gains and other nonrecurring items, operating net income available to common shareholders(1) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $22.3 million, or $0.90 per diluted share, up 211% from operating net income available to common shareholders(1) of $7.2 million, or $0.29 per diluted share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Commenting on the results, Dennis J. Zember, Jr., President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, stated, "The progress we have made over the past year is substantial.  A core margin of 3.59% with expansion of 14 basis points linked-quarter is a testament to the value of our Core Bank franchise which continues to drive slow and steady growth at attractive margins.  Our core earnings engine delivered a solid quarter in the face of unprecedented headwinds that reduced our retail mortgage pipeline 37% and reduced revenue by $2.3 million versus the second quarter. In a steady environment for retail mortgage, we would have been at our 1.00% ROAA target this quarter as expected.   We are already making changes to close the gap during this period of lower volumes while preserving our ability to benefit when volumes eventually recover."
The Company demonstrated strong profitability in the third quarter and year-to-date in 2026.  Significant areas of improvement year-over-year are detailed in the chart below:
As of or for the Three MonthsEnded September 30
As of or for the Nine Months Ended September 30

The third quarter of 2026 demonstrated continued progress across the Company's strategies to meet its growth and profitability goals in 2026. The following discussion highlights recent progress for each of these strategies:

The Core Bank's 24 banking offices in Virginia and Maryland represent almost two-thirds of the Company's total balance sheet and are a vital source of attractive lending and core funding.  Recent activity in the Core Bank includes the following:
The Core Bank has low concentrations of investor CRE (24% of total loans and only 188% of regulatory capital).
Core Bank loan growth of 11% annualized in the third quarter of 2026 with a pipeline of $160 million as of September 30, 2026.
Cost of deposits of 1.63% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.73% in the same quarter in 2025.
Approximately 21% of the Core Bank's deposits are noninterest bearing.

The Core Bank's deposit base is supported by what management believes is the region's best and most unique technology including the Bank's proprietary and recently rebranded Banking Valet service.  Over 87% of Banking Valet users are commercial customers and clients who actively use the service have average relationship balances of almost $1 million.

Primis Mortgage had closed mortgage volume of $347 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 12.5% compared to the same quarter in 2025, in spite of significant macroeconomic headwinds in the third quarter of 2026.  Construction-to-permanent loan volume was $40.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $26.4 million in the same period in 2025.  Pre-tax losses related to Primis Mortgage were approximately $0.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, down from earnings of $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Mortgage warehouse lending showed resilience in the third quarter of 2026 in the face of substantial market disruption.  Outstanding loan balances at September 30, 2026 were $501 million, down 8% from $544 million at June 30, 2026 and up 53% from $327 million at September 30, 2025.  Average loan balances were $427 million in the third quarter of 2026, up slightly from $426 million in the second quarter of 2026 and up 103% from $210 million in the third quarter of 2025.  Mortgage warehouse also funded on average approximately 11% of its balance sheet with associated customer noninterest bearing deposit balances during the third quarter of 2026.

Panacea's growth remained strong through the third quarter of 2026 with loans outstanding of $642 million, including loans held for sale, up 17% annualized compared to June 30, 2026.  Panacea sold approximately $32 million of loans in the third quarter of 2026 and had $39 million of loans classified as held for sale at September 30, 2026.  Panacea loans held for investment were $603 million at September 30, 2026, up 14% annualized from $583 million at June 30, 2026.  At the end of the third quarter of 2026, Panacea customer deposits totaled $207 million, up 56% from September 30, 2025.  Panacea remains the number one ranked "Bank for doctors" on Google and serves over 7,500 professionals and practices nationwide.

Our highly scalable digital platform continues to provide attractive funding for the Bank's nationwide business lines while protecting the Bank's low cost in-market funding.  The platform ended the third quarter of 2026 with approximately $1.0 billion of deposits with a cost of deposits of 3.80% compared to $1.0 billion at September 30, 2025 with a cost of 4.07%.  The platform also successfully grew business accounts in 2026 with small business balances reaching $54 million at September 30, 2026, up substantially from $16 million at December 31, 2025. These customers remain loyal with approximately 76% of our digital deposits banking with Primis for at least three years.

Net interest income in the third quarter of 2026 was $36.3 million, up 25%, from $29.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Included in interest income in the third quarter of 2026 was approximately $0.7 million of interest recoveries from a previously charged off loan. Adjusting for the recovery, net interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $35.6 million, up 23% from the prior year period.  Net interest margin was 3.66%, or 3.59% adjusted for the interest recovery, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 3.18% in the same quarter of 2025 with the expansion driven by robust earning asset growth funded at attractive incremental margins.

Yield on earnings assets in the third quarter of 2026 increased 22 basis points and 30 basis points versus the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively, including approximately 7 basis points due to the interest recovery noted above.  Yield on investments increased 135 basis points year-over-year largely due to the portfolio restructuring in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Cost of deposits in the Bank have benefitted from the focus on growing noninterest bearing deposit balances as well as the Core Bank's management of interest expense. In the third quarter of 2026, the Company reported cost of interest-bearing deposits of 2.70% compared to 2.88% in the same quarter in 2025. Cost of funds was 2.47% in the third quarter of 2026, down 15 basis points from 2.62% in the third quarter of 2025.

Noninterest income was $12.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $22.0 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $12.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Mortgage related income decreased 10% to $8.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $8.9 million in the same quarter in 2025. In 2026, the Company restructured its bank-owned life insurance portfolio which improved noninterest income by approximately $0.4 million per quarter beginning late in the second quarter of 2026.  Lastly, the third quarter of 2026 benefited from $0.9 million of recoveries from a previously charged-off loan and $0.4 million in payouts from a bank-owned life insurance policy.

The Company reported gain on sale income of $1.5 million related to the sale of Panacea loans and the guaranteed portion of SBA loans in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.  Approximately $0.5 million of the gain on sale income was attributable to the Core Bank in the third quarter of 2026 with the remainder driven by the Panacea Division.

Noninterest expense was $37.2 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $32.3 million for the same quarter of 2025. The following table reflects the core operating expense burden at the Company, net of mortgage related and Panacea division impacts.

Core operating expense burden, as defined above, was $24.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 versus $24.9 million and $21.6 million in the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively.  As previously disclosed, all three quarters of 2026 include a full quarter of lease expense, net of reduced depreciation expense, of approximately $1.4 million from the Company's sale leaseback transaction executed in the fourth quarter of 2025.  The third quarter of 2026 also included approximately $1.4 million of loan related expenses and approximately $0.4 million of professional fees and other third-party expenses.  Excluding these expenses, core operating expense burden for the third quarter of 2026 would have been essentially flat with the second quarter of 2026 run rate and lower than the same period in 2025 when adjusting for net lease expense. As disclosed in the second quarter of 2026, the Company expects approximately $3.0 million of annualized savings from vendor consolidation and statement services beginning early in 2027.

Loans held for investment were $3.5 billion at September 30, 2026, flat compared to June 30, 2026 and increased 9% compared to $3.2 billion at September 30, 2025. Primary drivers of these changes include:
Core Bank loans ended slightly over $2.0 billion at September 30, 2026, up 11% annualized from June 30, 2026.
Panacea Financial loans, excluding loans held for sale, grew $20 million, or 3%, from June 30, 2026 to $603 million at September 30, 2026.

Mortgage warehouse balances decreased to $501 million at September 30, 2026 compared to $544 million at June 30, 2026. Average loan balances were $427 million in the third quarter of 2026, up slightly from $426 million in the second quarter of 2026.
Mortgage portfolio loans generated by Primis Mortgage grew to $156 million at September 30, 2026, up 10% from $140 million at June 30, 2026 and up 87% from $84 million at September 30, 2025.
Loan balances associated with the consumer loan program declined to $69 million at September 30, 2026, net of fair value discounts, compared to $101 million at September 30, 2025.

Nonperforming assets, excluding portions guaranteed by the SBA, improved to 1.43% of total assets at September 30, 2026 compared to 1.45% at June 30, 2026 and 2.07% at September 30, 2025. The Company continues to make progress reducing nonperforming assets with total nonperforming assets excluding SBA guaranteed balances decreasing to $61 million at September 30, 2026 from $63 million at June 30, 2026, representing a 3% reduction in the third quarter of 2026.

The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $1.1 million for the third quarter of 2026 compared to a provision for credit losses of $5.5 million for the second quarter of 2026 and a recovery of credit losses of $49 thousand for the third quarter of 2025.  The majority of the provision expense was driven by growth in the loan portfolio in the third quarter of 2026.  Core net charge-offs as a percentage of average loans were 17 basis points, up 14 basis points from the same period a year ago and down 36 basis points from the second quarter of 2026.  The increase in net charge-offs was largely driven by one credit that had previously been reserved for.  As a percentage of loans held for investment, the allowance for credit losses was 1.30% at the end of the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.40% at the end of the third quarter of 2025.

Total deposits at September 30, 2026 were $3.5 billion, up $0.1 billion, or 4% when compared to the same period in 2025. Noninterest bearing demand deposits were $496 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of 1% compared to balances at September 30, 2025. Average noninterest bearing deposits were $542 million in the third quarter of 2026, up 13% from $482 million in the third quarter of 2025. The Company had FHLB advances totaling $220 million outstanding at September 30, 2026, down from $300 million at June 30, 2026 and up from $85 million at September 30, 2025.  Average FHLB advances were $89 million in the third quarter of 2026, down from $133 million in the second quarter of 2026 and up from $1 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Tangible book value per common share(1) at the end of the third quarter of 2026 was $13.81, an increase of $2.10, or 18%, from levels reported at September 30, 2025. Tangible common equity(1) ended the third quarter of 2026 at $342.4 million, or 8.14% of tangible assets(1).
The Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.10 per share payable on November 20, 2026 to shareholders of record on November 6, 2026.  This is Primis' sixtieth consecutive quarterly dividend.

As of September 30, 2026, Primis had $4.3 billion in total assets, $3.5 billion in total loans held for investment and $3.5 billion in total deposits. Primis Bank provides a range of financial services to individuals and small- and medium-sized businesses through 24 full-service branches in Virginia and Maryland and provides services to customers through certain online and mobile applications.
Dennis J. Zember, Jr., President and CEO
Matthew A. Switzer, EVP and CFO
Primis Financial Corp., NASDAQ Symbol FRST
